question: What is the chemical formula for potassium permanganate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**KMnO₄**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Potassium permanganate has the chemical formula **KMnO₄**, consisting of potassium (K), manganese (Mn), and oxygen (O).
 
• It is a dark purple crystalline compound widely used as a **strong oxidizing agent** in chemical reactions.
 
• KMnO₄ readily dissolves in water to form potassium ions (K⁺) and permanganate ions (MnO₄−).
 
• The manganese in KMnO₄ has an oxidation state of **+7**, which contributes to its oxidizing properties.
 
• Potassium permanganate is used in **water treatment, disinfection, and various oxidation reactions in organic and inorganic chemistry.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidizing Properties of KMnO₄:**

 
 
• In acidic conditions, KMnO₄ reduces to Mn²⁺, releasing oxygen and acting as a strong oxidizer.
 
• In neutral or alkaline mediums, it reduces to MnO₂ (manganese dioxide).
 
• Its oxidizing ability is useful in redox titrations and industrial applications.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Potassium Permanganate:**
 
 
• It is used for **purifying and disinfecting water** by oxidizing organic impurities and iron or manganese in water.
 
• Medicinally, it is employed as an antiseptic for treating skin conditions like fungal infections and wounds.
 
• In organic chemistry, KMnO₄ is used to oxidize alkenes to glycols and alcohols to carboxylic acids.
 
 
 
• **Structure of Permanganate Ion:**
 
 
• The permanganate ion (MnO₄−) has a tetrahedral geometry.
 
• Manganese is surrounded by four oxygen atoms, with double-bond character distributed via resonance.
 
 
 
• **Safety Considerations:**
 
 
• KMnO₄ is a strong oxidizer and can ignite combustible materials upon contact.
 
• Direct contact can cause skin irritation and permanent stains, while ingestion is toxic and harmful.
 
• It should be stored in a cool, dry place, away from organic materials to prevent decomposition.
